covers.quote: You should also make sure the content is available in another format, such as HTML.

rules.quote: HTML should be the default format for all government information.
rules.violation_condition: government report or information published only in non-HTML formats without HTML as the primary format
rules.why: Clear modality instruction on default publishing format (G-4).

rules.quote: You must make all government content accessible to people with disability.
rules.violation_condition: government report content that is not accessible to people with disability
rules.why: Explicit statutory requirement stated with 'must'.

rules.quote: You must produce documents in line with parliamentary printing standards. Electronic versions must be identical to printed versions and must be accessible.
rules.violation_condition: documents tabled in parliament that do not meet parliamentary printing standards, or whose electronic versions differ from printed versions or are inaccessible
when: When documents are to be included in the Parliamentary Papers Series / tabled in Parliament.
rules.why: Mandatory requirement governing documents tabled in parliament.

rules.quote: Australian Government annual reports must be tabled in the Australian Parliament.
rules.violation_condition: Australian Government annual report that is not tabled in Parliament
when: Applies specifically to Australian Government annual reports.
rules.why: Mandatory publication/tabling requirement for annual reports.

rules.quote: Australian Government departments and agencies must also publish their annual reports through the Transparency Portal.
rules.violation_condition: an annual report of an Australian Government department or agency not published through the Transparency Portal
when: Applies to annual reports of Australian Government departments and agencies.
rules.why: Mandatory publishing requirement for agency annual reports.

rules.quote: You must use the Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) when preparing government information.
rules.violation_condition: government information or reports prepared without following the PSPF for classification and marking
rules.why: Mandatory compliance instruction regarding PSPF.

rules.quote: You must follow your organisation’s information management requirements.
rules.violation_condition: records and reports not managed or disposed of according to organisational information management requirements under the Archives Act 1983
rules.why: Mandatory compliance requirement under the Archives Act 1983.

rules.quote: The words always run across or down the spine.
rules.violation_condition: text on a report dust jacket spine running upwards rather than across or down
when: When the dust jacket spine is more than about 5 millimetres wide.
rules.why: Direct layout rule for spine text on printed works.

rules.quote: Australian Government reports published online should include the same information as a printed version.
rules.violation_condition: an online Australian Government report that omits preliminary content or information present in its printed counterpart
rules.why: Normative instruction on online reports matching print counterparts.

covers.quote: name of the sponsor, if applicable.

rules.quote:
A title page should include the following:

- title
- subtitle, if any
- author’s name
- name of the sponsor, if applicable.
rules.violation_condition: a title page missing the title, author's name, or applicable subtitle/sponsor
when: Subtitle is only included if applicable.
Sponsor name is only included if applicable.
rules.why: Specifies required items on a title page (G-2).

rules.quote: Show the main title exactly as it appears on the cover.
rules.violation_condition: a half-title page where the main title does not exactly match the title on the cover
when: Applies to half-title pages in printed reports.
rules.why: Instruction on half-title page wording.

rules.quote: Do not show any subtitles.
rules.violation_condition: subtitles appearing on a half-title page
when: Applies to half-title pages in printed reports.
rules.why: Clear negative instruction for half-title pages.

rules.quote: Number them with lower case roman numerals such as ’i’, ’ii’, ’iii’ and ’iv’.
rules.violation_condition: preliminary pages of a report numbered using something other than lower-case roman numerals
when: Applies to preliminary pages of a report.
rules.why: Specific numbering convention for preliminary pages.

rules.quote: You must choose a licence to release copyright materials. If you work in government, use an open access licence if you can (for example, Creative Commons).
rules.violation_condition: government copyright materials published without an explicitly chosen licence
rules.why: Mandatory requirement for licensing copyright material in reports.

covers.quote: the signature of the person responsible for the report
the day, month and year the report was submitted.

rules.quote:
The letter of transmittal must include the purpose of the report and who it is for. It must have:

- the signature of the person responsible for the report
- the day, month and year the report was submitted.
rules.violation_condition: a letter of transmittal missing the purpose, the recipient, the signature of the responsible person, or the submission date (day, month, year)
when: When a letter of transmittal is included in a report.
rules.why: Explicit 'must' requirements for transmittal letters (G-2).

rules.quote: Use the heading ‘Contents’, not ‘Table of contents’ or ‘List of contents’.
rules.violation_condition: contents list headed with 'Table of contents' or 'List of contents' instead of 'Contents'
rules.why: Strict heading naming convention.

rules.quote:
The order of lists is:

1. photographs (only in print)
2. figures
3. maps (if listed separately)
4. tables.
rules.violation_condition: lists of images and tables ordered contrary to: photographs, figures, maps, tables
when: Photographs only in print.
Maps if listed separately.
rules.why: Strict ordering rule for illustration lists (G-2).

rules.quote: Don't use ‘Executive summary’. Although this is common, it is not best practice.
rules.violation_condition: report summary section headed or referred to as 'Executive summary'
rules.why: Explicit negative prohibition on heading terminology.

rules.quote: Use consecutive numbering for chapter titles through the report. If the report contains parts, continue the chapter numbering into each part.
rules.violation_condition: chapter numbering restarting within parts or not running consecutively throughout the report
when: Applies when chapters are numbered, including when grouped into parts.
rules.why: Clear structural numbering instruction.

rules.quote: Don't use roman numerals to number parts.
rules.violation_condition: roman numerals used to number parts in a report (e.g. 'Part II')
rules.why: Direct negative instruction regarding numbering format.

rules.quote: Page numbering for the endmatter continues from the main body of the report.
rules.violation_condition: page numbering restarting or switching schemes for the endmatter in a single-volume printed report
rules.why: Page numbering rule for endmatter.

rules.quote: Number appendices differently from how chapters are numbered in the report.
rules.violation_condition: appendices numbered using the same numeral style as chapters (e.g. arabic numbers for both)
rules.why: Differentiation rule for numbering appendices.

rules.quote: Do not incorporate the list of shortened forms in the glossary.
rules.violation_condition: shortened forms/abbreviations incorporated directly into the glossary instead of kept as a separate list
rules.why: Explicit negative instruction.

rules.quote: List glossary items in alphabetical order.
rules.violation_condition: glossary items not presented in alphabetical order
rules.why: Ordering rule for glossaries.

rules.quote: Always place a bibliography after a reference list or endnotes if the report has both.
rules.violation_condition: bibliography placed before a reference list or endnotes when both appear
when: Applies when the report contains both a bibliography and a reference list or endnotes.
rules.why: Direct ordering rule with 'Always'.

rules.quote: Each volume should have a summary list of the contents of the other volumes in the set.
rules.violation_condition: a volume in a multi-volume report missing a summary list of the contents of the other volumes
when: Applies when a report is split into multiple volumes.
rules.why: Structural requirement for multi-volume reports.

rules.quote: Always number preliminary pages per volume.
rules.violation_condition: preliminary page numbering continuing across multiple volumes rather than restarting per volume
when: Applies to printed multi-volume reports.
rules.why: Clear imperative instruction on numbering multi-volume preliminary pages.
